subject.title: Inconsistent message:sent / message_sent hook coverage across multiple outbound dispatch paths

question: Should outbound lifecycle hook parity be solved through one canonical core observer/plugin-SDK delivery-report seam, or through independently reviewed channel and surface-specific fixes?
rationale: The remaining gaps cross public Plugin SDK behavior, security/audit observers, and channel streaming semantics, so automation should not choose the permanent hook contract or exception policy without maintainer direction.

options.title: Canonical observer/report seam
options.body: Make one core-owned sent/sending reporting contract and require channels plus Gateway/TUI/HTTP surfaces to use it or explicitly document why they cannot.

options.title: Channel-local parity fixes
options.body: Review and land narrow PRs for Telegram, msteams, WhatsApp, Gateway, and TUI independently, accepting higher risk of semantic drift.

options.title: Document limited support
options.body: Keep outbound lifecycle hooks best-effort by surface and document unsupported paths, leaving security and audit plugins with weaker guarantees.

recommendation.title: Canonical observer/report seam
recommendation.body: Make one core-owned sent/sending reporting contract and require channels plus Gateway/TUI/HTTP surfaces to use it or explicitly document why they cannot.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice spans core, plugin, Gateway, and channel boundaries, and steipete is the clearest current cross-boundary review/merge signal in the available history.
